items.abstract_or_text: ui : Discover & Download Models from HF Hub (#29584) * common : resolve - download tags and list cached sidecars A Q4_0-mtp style tag now resolves the sidecar file when no model file matches it, so a solo draft or mmproj download actually pulls the file. Cached sidecar files list as their own entries so the state survives a restart, and removing such a tag deletes only the sidecar. Assisted-by: pi:zai-org/GLM-5.3 * ui : optional sanitized raw HTML in markdown Add an allowHtml prop to MarkdownContent: raw HTML found in the markdown is rendered after DOMPurify sanitization instead of being escaped as literal text. Default stays escaped. Assisted-by: pi:GLM-5.3-Flash * ui : add the discover models components The Discover surface: the curated-catalog list with its search and skeletons, the details pane with its readme, metadata, Hub stats and download options, and the standalone download progress bar that replaces the plain one. items.abstract_or_text: tests: give the random model generator a per-tensor filler table (#30674) * tests: give the random model generator a per-tensor filler table Muse Spark makes test-llama-context fail on state_load, cp_h and cp_d on about six percent of the random seeds, with an NMSE of 1.0e-05 to 1.4e-05 against a threshold of 1.0e-05. The sliding window is what exposes it: a restored state keeps the window alone, so the attention of an SWA layer reduces over a different cell layout and the continuation is not bit exact. Every SWA model carries that, at 1e-08. Muse Spark carried it at 1e-05. The generator is what turns 1e-08 into 1e-05. A norm preserving residual gate holds alpha^2 + beta^2 == 1 and the conversion resolves both weights from one raw weight, while the generator draws every tensor on its own. The pair then scaled the stream and the branch independently, the stream lost an arbitrary factor at each layer, and the model became an amplifier. The weights the test ran on were not a Muse Spark. Per-tensor rules lived inside the write path, where a flag picked the values of a tensor inside each of the two branches that store them, so a new rule meant a new flag threaded through both. The file asks to be rid of that in a TODO of its own. Give each rule a filler, pick one from a table keyed on a substring of the tensor name, and keep a single write path behind it. Mamba moves into the table and Muse Spark joins it: the gate filler draws the raw weight once per block and resolves alpha and beta the way the conversion does. Over a thousand seeds on a CPU build the worst case drops from 1.36e-05 to 2.48e-06 and the median from 4.10e-06 to 5.48e-07, with no seed above the threshold. The other 131 models come out identical to the bit, since no other architecture carries these tensors. ctest is green on a CPU build and on a CUDA build. * tests: draw every tensor filler from fill_normal The fillers repeated the generator and the distribution each time. The normal draw now takes its key and the other fillers transform its values, so the generator lives in one place. The generated models are identical to the bit. **Website:** - **Attestations:** - **macOS/iOS:** - [macOS Apple Silicon (arm64)](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/download/b11712/llama-b11712-bin-macos-arm64.tar.gz) - items.abstract_or_text: model : add Kolibri-1 (Aleph-Alpha) support (#30673) * model : add Kolibri-1 (Aleph-Alpha) support Kolibri-1 is a bilingual German/English MoE reasoning model with 78B parameters and 3.46B active per token: 50 layers, 384 routed experts plus one shared expert. Attention interleaves four sliding layers at a 513 window with one full layer. The sliding layers rotate with NeoX RoPE, the full layers are NoPE. GQA runs 48 query heads against 4 KV heads at head_dim 128 with a QK-RMSNorm, and every block carries four RMSNorms, so the attention and the MLP output are normalized before they rejoin the residual stream. Routing picks the experts from logits + expert_bias and weights them with the sigmoid of the unbiased logits, without renorm. The converter reuses AfmoeModel for the per-expert checkpoint layout and the expert selection bias, and writes the shared expert and the per layer sliding window pattern. The released FP8 checkpoint needs no special code, it goes through the generic weight_scale_inv path. Three tensor names are added to the mapping (post_attn_norm, post_ffn_norm, moe.router.expert_bias) and the 128k vocabulary registers the qwen2 pre-tokenizer by hash. The arch is registered in test-llama-archs, with GQA and the sliding window pattern. items.abstract_or_text: model : Granite switch decision 256 options (#30693) * feat(convert): Attempt to come up with 256 single-token, semantic option markers Each switch model needs to identify a collection of single-token option markers that can be mapped to their respective logits for the output probability distribution. The simple upper/lower/numbers set only yields 66 unique markers, but the model can support up to 255. The challenge is that which combinations of characters result in single-token markers is model- specific, so we do a discovery exercise at conversion time by looking through the specific model's vocab for single-token sequences of 1+ plain letter strings (eg `A`, `AA`, `BB`, etc). items.abstract_or_text: hexagon: vectorize softplus with HVX (#30435) softplus_f32 and tile_softplus_f32 ran a scalar logf(1.0f + expf(x)) loop. Replace both with a shared hvx_softplus_f32_aa() helper built from the backend's existing hvx_vec_exp_f32 / hvx_vec_log_f32 primitives, so no new numerical approximation is introduced. hvx_vec_exp_f32 clamps its input to (-88, 88) before exponentiating, so a naive log(1 + exp(x)) composition would saturate to ~88.72 for large x instead of returning x. The Q6_V_vmux_QVV select keeps the scalar reference's x > 20 guard (ggml_compute_softplus_f32 in ggml-impl.h), which is what makes the vector path match the CPU result. items.abstract_or_text: common: honor HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY env vars in http client (#21752) * common: honor HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY env vars in http client common_http_client() was ignoring standard proxy env vars, causing downloads via -hf and similar flags to fail silently in environments behind an HTTP proxy (corporate networks, air-gapped infra, etc.). Checks HTTPS_PROXY/https_proxy for https:// URLs and HTTP_PROXY/http_proxy for http:// URLs, in that order. If a proxy URL is set and parseable, passes it to httplib's set_proxy() and set_proxy_basic_auth() as appropriate. Malformed proxy URLs are silently ignored so existing callers aren't affected. Fixes #21694 * common: drop misleading comment about generic proxy fallback The comment referenced a 'generic one' that doesn't exist in the code — both HTTP_PROXY and HTTPS_PROXY are scheme-specific. Reviewer noted the mismatch. Addresses review feedback from @ServeurpersoCom. * common : warn when the proxy URL from the environment is malformed * common : honor NO_PROXY when selecting the http proxy * ci : retrigger checks (test-thread-safety flake) * common : bypass the proxy for loopback destinations llama cli talks to its spawned server on 127.0.0.1 through common_http_client, so with HTTP_PROXY set and no NO_PROXY the health polling went to the corporate proxy, which rejects loopback targets, and the wait loop never exits ("Loading model..." hangs forever). A remote proxy can never reach the client machine's own loopback, so these destinations are now always contacted directly, before NO_PROXY is consulted: localhost, *.localhost, 127.0.0.0/8, ::1 and 0.0.0.0. Similar to Go's net/http. Proxy handling for downloads and remote --server-base endpoints is unchanged.
